post.caption: Millefiori glass sometimes hides tiny faces. Millefiori is Italian for a thousand flowers. Makers bundle colored glass rods and stretch them into a long bar. The bar is cut across, and every slice shows the same flower. Slices laid in a disc are heated until they melt together. Alexandria was a leading center for this glass over 2,000 years ago. Venice used it by the 1400s and revived it in the 1800s. Murano makers put tiny portraits inside canes, so slices show faces. One slice from the 1840s shows a man in uniform. Millefiori paperweights became a craze in the mid 1840s.
